candidate_relations.reason: The ECG shows a narrow QRS tachycardia, which is consistent with SVT as a broad class. However, the reference diagnosis specifies accelerated AV junctional tachycardia with isorhythmic AV dissociation — a distinct subtype characterized by independent but near-equal atrial and ventricular rates, varying PR intervals, cannon waves, and variable S1. C001 captures only the parent morphological category without the required mechanistic specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: SVT with narrow QRS is the parent category; missing the specific subtype (accelerated AV junctional tachycardia) and the key mechanistic feature (isorhythmic AV dissociation with cannon waves and varying PR intervals)

case_quality_flags: ECG description explicitly documents isorhythmic AV dissociation (near-equal P and QRS rates with varying PR intervals), cannon waves on JVP, and variable S1 — all hallmarks of accelerated AV junctional tachycardia; diagnosis is well-supported by the record
